"issue-150" (2026-10-05T21:07:43Z) — 5 section(s):

[1] "issue-150" section 1:
Issue #150 in re-cinq/Otto: Stop echoing the access token in the WebSocket handshake response
State: closed
Author: gedaiu
Labels: size:S, area:compliance, area:auth, repo:hal-engine, epic:E2, type:bug
Opened: 2026-08-21T13:58:45Z
Closed: 2026-10-05T21:07:43Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/issues/150

Part of #56

## Why

The protocol tells every client to send its access token as the WebSocket subprotocol, and the server echoes the first offered subprotocol straight back. `ws` writes whatever is returned into the 101 response headers and holds it as a live property on every connected socket object. The documented rationale claims this avoids exposure in server logs, which is only half true: the token is out of the request line (so out of a URL-based access log) but sits in the **response** headers, where an ingress log with header capture, a proxy trace, or a debug `console.log(ws)` picks it up. This was found while building `091`, which depends on `handleProtocols` continuing to work and deliberately left it unchanged.

[2] "issue-150" section 2:
## What to do

Add a reserved marker subprotocol constant (`HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL = 'hal.v1'`, in a new `src/transport/ws/subprotocol.ts`, re-exported from the package root) and change `createServer`'s `handleProtocols` to select the marker when the client offers it, rather than blindly echoing the first offered value. A client now offers two values - `hal.v1, <access-token>` - and the server always answers `hal.v1`, so the credential is never a candidate for the response header while still reaching the server (`bearerFromWebSocketProtocol` reads the **request** header, which is unaffected). Simply refusing to echo anything was measured and rejected: both `ws`'s own client and Chromium refuse a handshake where the server answers a non-empty subprotocol offer with nothing at all, so a marker is required, not just a smaller response. `bearerFromWebSocketProtocol` now selects the first **non-marker** value regardless of offer order, narrowing `091`'s existing "first offered subprotocol is the credential" rule. Update the protocol doc's client contract and security-rationale sections to describe the two-value offer, the character-set constraint (a subprotocol is validated client-side as an HTTP token, so padded base64 tokens can't use this carrier at all), and what the carrier does and doesn't protect against.

[3] "issue-150" section 3:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL = 'hal.v1'` is exported from `src/transport/ws/subprotocol.ts` and re-exported from the package root
- [ ] `handleProtocols` returns the marker when offered and `false` otherwise - a test asserts `false` for an offer containing only a bare token
- [ ] A real upgrade offering `hal.v1, super-secret-token` receives a 101 response whose `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header is exactly `hal.v1`, with the token string appearing in no response header
- [ ] The connected socket's `protocol` property is `'hal.v1'` - no live object holds the credential
- [ ] `bearerFromWebSocketProtocol` returns the credential for both `hal.v1, <token>` and `<token>, hal.v1` orderings, and `undefined` when only the marker is offered
- [ ] A client offering only the marker still connects successfully, reading the credential from the `Authorization` header if present
- [ ] A client offering a bare token with no marker receives a 101 with no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header at all
- [ ] The protocol doc's client contract shows the two-value offer, states the server echoes only the marker, and states the HTTP-token character-set constraint on what a subprotocol-carried value can contain

[4] "issue-150" section 4:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The security-rationale section no longer claims unqualified log-exposure avoidance, and names the remaining request-header exposure
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md`'s matching sentence is updated to the same two-value description
- [ ] A test asserts the exported constant matches the literal printed in the docs
- [ ] **GDPR.** No value offered in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` is written to any log at any level across the whole connection lifecycle, including the close handler
- [ ] **NIS-2 Article 21 access control.** The doc's security section lists every place a credential exists during a connection (request headers, session storage, tool context), so an operator configuring log redaction has a complete list to work from
- [ ] A spec exists at `specs/hal-engine-subprotocol-marker/spec.md` with `([validated by ...])` links
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` and `npm test` pass

[5] "issue-150" section 5:
## Tech notes

Measured against `ws@8.20.0`/Node v20.19.5: answering a non-empty subprotocol offer with nothing throws a client- side error in both `ws` and Chromium, which is why a marker (not a bare refusal) is the fix. No deprecation window is needed - the package is unpublished (`0.1.0`) and neither live consumer sends a subprotocol at all today (`the-expert` authenticates via a query parameter on its own transport; `the-expert-ui` opens its socket with no subprotocol argument).

Out of scope: which credential wins when the `Authorization` header and the subprotocol disagree (`091`'s territory), which captured headers reach a tool (`088`), a client offering the marker plus two non-marker values (the first non-marker value wins, matching today's behavior - making an ambiguous offer a hard refusal is `091`'s call), verifying the handshake in a real browser (no browser in this repo's CI), and reading a session id from the upgrade request (`081`).

Build with `/lore-feature "Stop echoing the access token in the WebSocket handshake response"` - spec lands at `specs/hal-engine-subprotocol-marker/spec.md`, tasks at `tasks.md`, description via `/lore-pr`.
